Build a production-quality demo marketing website for a real local hair salons & suites business in Beaverton, OR. Let someone book an appointment and leave a deposit at 10pm without speaking to anybody. I will show it to the owner in a sales conversation, so it must look finished and be honest about what is real.

Constraints — do not break these
1. Invent nothing. No fabricated reviews, testimonials, client names, licence numbers, years in business, awards, certifications, insurance details or statistics. Where I have not supplied content, render a visible placeholder such as [REVIEW 1 — pull from Google profile] rather than plausible filler.
2. Never use the prospect's own photos without their written permission. Until I tell you I hold it, every photo slot uses public/placeholder.svg, clearly marked as a placeholder on the page. Once I do, use only the images I supply. No stock photography, no AI-generated photos of work.
3. Render a small line in the footer: "Demo site — not affiliated with {Business Name}." I remove it once they pay.
4. Do not use their logo unless I supply the file. Set the wordmark in type instead.
5. Do not add analytics, tracking pixels, cookie banners or third-party scripts to the demo.
6. No horizontal page scroll at any viewport from 320px up.
7. Do not invent prices, durations or availability. A wrong price on a booking page produces an angry customer, not a lead.
8. Do not publish staff names, photographs or credentials I have not supplied.
9. If the booking provider is not chosen yet, render the widget as a clearly marked placeholder listing the fields it will need.
10. Do not fork the theme system. If this trade genuinely needs a colour the palette lacks, tell me and propose a different themeId — never hard-code a hex in a component.

Copy direction
- Headline formula: the offering plus the city, plainly. The home page targets the phrase "hair salon Beaverton".
- Tone: Calm, spacious and personal. Written by the practitioner, not an agency.
- Plain English, short sentences, no marketing adjectives, no "we pride ourselves on".
- Every call to action offers the same two options: "Book now" or "See availability".
- Write real FAQ answers for this specific trade. Where a number is required and I have not supplied it, use a bracketed placeholder.

Technical requirements
- Mobile-first. Design for a 390px phone held one-handed, then scale up.
- Lighthouse mobile: performance 90+, accessibility 95+. LCP under 2.5s on simulated slow 4G.
- All images through next/image with explicit sizes, priority on the hero only, lazy below the fold.
- Extend the template's JSON-LD to: The closest LocalBusiness subtype (HealthAndBeautyBusiness, AutoRepair, AnimalShelter as applicable) plus Service with offers.price and OpeningHoursSpecification.
- Text contrast 4.5:1 minimum, visible :focus-visible rings, real alt text, one h1 per route, prefers-reduced-motion respected.

Done when
- pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint and pnpm build all pass clean, and pnpm dev runs with no console errors or hydration warnings.
- Changing site.config.ts alone swaps the business name, city, phone, hours and theme everywhere, with no component edits.
- /style-guide renders the chosen theme and /demo-shots renders the new sections.
- Every unsupplied fact renders as a visible bracketed placeholder — searching the built page for "[" finds all of them.
- I can complete a booking end-to-end on a 390px screen without making a phone call.
- Every service in the menu shows a price and a duration, or a visible bracketed placeholder.

Size of the ask
Do not do this in one pass. Four reviewable steps, stop and report after each:
1. Create from the template, pnpm install, read CLAUDE.md, fill site.config.ts including themeId 'C35', confirm /style-guide.
2. Adapt the 3 reused template sections to this business, static content only.
3. Build the 8 new section components and wire the online booking flow end to end through deliverContactForm().
4. Add the remaining routes, extend the JSON-LD, then a Lighthouse pass and fixes.

- Bridal and event hair: Trial appointment booking, on-location fees, party size, timing on the day, and the deposit that holds the date (Wedding hair is booked months ahead with a trial, and brides compare stylists on how organised the process looks.)
- Curly and textured hair specialties: Curly cuts, textured hair, silk press, protective styles, what to arrive with and how long each service takes (People with curly or textured hair search specifically for a stylist who knows their hair, and leave a salon that can't say so.)
